A knowledge base on running Google Business Profiles into subcontracted trade work, reached through the

> told. One rejection story is an anecdote, never a requirement.

# The playbook as a manual: derived trust, a digest per capture, one tree

## Why

The repo is a framework for turning recordings into a manual an agent answers from. Three things
keep it from being one:

1. **`knowledge/structured/` is a heap of anecdotes filed by funnel stage.** Bullets read "X said Y on
   a call": sources, not conclusions. The `info / facts / plays` split files one topic three ways by
   *kind of statement*. `approved/` and `suggested/` are twin trees, so no page can be rewritten into
   something coherent: half of every topic lives in the other tree. `guides/` then re-states the same
   claims a third time, by hand.
2. **Trust is partly hand-computed.** A citation's `r<n>` is a number someone looked up in a table and
   typed; it goes stale when the table moves. The score is `base + age/180d`: additive, linear,
   lower-is-better. For calls the server does not know who speaks, so the member skill is told to add
   two numbers itself. The date is when a thing was *said*, never when it was *true*.
3. **A capture goes straight from transcript to scattered bullets.** There is no reading of a source
   as a whole, so `knowledge/references/` is unusable except through search, and what a call said is
   only recoverable from where its fragments were scattered.

Text is code with no compiler. Wherever a rule below can be checked, `playbook check` checks it and
the build fails on it; a rule that cannot be checked goes to `docs/spec/`.

**No patches.** Each part is implemented in the shape described, not approximated by a shim over the
old one: no parser accepting both formats, no fallback score, no directory kept "for now". Finishing a
sub-task in a way that bends the design is worth nothing.

## Shape

```
 recording ──pull──► <capture>.md            raw: transcript, stamped per paragraph. never edited after the pull
     │                  │
     └──watch──► <capture>/shown.md          machine reading of the picture
                        │
              digest    ▼
                 <capture>/content.md        machine reading of the whole: chapters → attributed points
                        │
              propose   ▼
                 knowledge/log/digest/<date>-<capture>.md     what should move into the manual, and where
                        │
              integrate ▼
                 knowledge/structured/**     the manual: conclusions, evidence under them, unvetted marked `(?)`
                        │
              compile   ▼   (nix build; fails on any check)
                 index: every claim resolved to who · trust · date of the information
                        │
              query     ▼   (server, now)
                 effective = trust × γ(age)   printed as one number on every hit
```

## 1. Trust — `docs/spec/trust.md`

New spec, tracked with tracey (`/tracey` skill; the repo has no `.config/tracey` yet). The
`## Invariants` of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` move to `docs/spec/knowledge.md` beside it, restated for the
shape below, minus every one a check now forces. Rules, each one line:

- effective trust is `trust × γ(age)`, in `[0, 1]`, higher is better
- `trust = source(who) × grade(how)`: who said it, and whether they ran it, say it, or heard it
- `γ` is a power law, `γ(age) = (1 + age/τ)^-s`: steep early, long tail. `τ` and `s` are two constants
  in one place
- `age` counts from when the information was *observed*, not when it was said: the capture's date
  unless the speaker dates it earlier, never later. A manual citation always writes it, since a page
  mixes sources; a digest point writes it only when it differs from its capture's
- nothing derived from the trust tables or the clock is ever written into `knowledge/`, a skill or a
  tool description. Only the facts it derives from are: who, how they know, when
- no reader, human or model, is ever asked to do trust arithmetic: a hit carries its effective number
  or says it has none

Consequences:

- **Citation** carries facts, not a score: `<!--<date> <who> <how> <url>-->`, `how ∈ ran | says | heard`.
  `who` is omitted where the source fixes it (course, a youtube channel). The same line with no url is
  what `// unsourced: <who>` was; our own test is `us ran` and links the comment that closed its issue.
  The two tables, `source` and `grade`, live in `knowledge/README.md`: one people table carrying trust,
  the youtube channel (today a hand-kept `CHANNELS` in `corpus.rs`) and the `experts` data (reach,
  proven at, available) that `guides/experts.md` holds. Rescale the 0–7 bases to `(0, 1]` in order.
- **One trust model in code**, a module both `playbook` and `playbook_web` link, replacing
  `effective` in `cite_check.rs`, `effective`/`age` in `corpus.rs`, and `build.rs` grepping a constant
  out of another crate's source and tables out of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **One source identity.** `source_key` in `cite_check.rs` knows loom, fathom, chatgpt, youtube and
  skool; drive, vimeo, vocaroo and docs captures cannot be cited at all. Every capture is citable.
- **Compile.** `playbook check` grows into the compiler of the corpus: it resolves every citation and
  every digest point to `(who, trust, information date, source second)` and emits the index the server
  loads. `playbook_web/build.rs` runs it, so a release cannot be cut from a corpus that fails a check.
  The server applies `γ` at query time — a number stamped at build would be stale by the age of the
  release. The server stops parsing citations itself (`CITATION` in `corpus.rs` reads to the end of the
  chapter, so an unsourced bullet inherits its neighbour's score). `Kind::Approved`/`Suggested` become
  one kind, with vetted-or-not on the claim.
- **Calls.** A transcript line has no speaker, so it has no score; its hit says so and points at its
  chapter in `content.md`, whose points do. `plugin/skills/service-arb/SKILL.md`'s *Weighing* shrinks
  to: higher effective leads; unscored transcript is a quote, not a weight.

## 2. A digest per capture — `<capture>/content.md`

`<capture>.md` is raw and `<capture>/` holds machine readings of it, each naming what produced it —
one shape for every platform, youtube included (its `## summary`, `## chapters` and `## shown` are
written into the capture by the puller today).

This removes the one exception that let an agent write into a capture. Today `/ingest call-digest`
writes `## summary` there, titles some paragraph headers and deletes the rest, so a claim's exact
second is only recoverable from git history, and `check calls` diffs the prose against `HEAD` to prove
nothing else moved. Instead: a capture is never edited after its pull and keeps the finest stamp its
platform gives, per paragraph. What the platform itself wrote (summary, chapters) stays in it
verbatim, as input. Chapters we read into it live in `content.md`; `read` serves a chapter as its
points plus the transcript from its stamp to the next one's.

Fifteen calls already carry a digested `## summary` with topic chapters: those move out and gain
attribution, they are not redone from nothing.

```md
# <title>
- of: <capture> · digested by: <what>, <date>

## gist
who was on, what scale each operates at, what the call settled — a paragraph

## chapters
### [12:34](<url>?t=754) <topic>
- <point, in the speaker's terms; numbers, names, handles verbatim>
  <!--<who> <how> ?t=771-->
- Q: … / A: …

## open
questions nobody answered; things someone said they would do
```

No public prompt of Loom's or Fathom's exists; the skeleton above is theirs (purpose → topics with
seek links → open items) plus attribution. Two things carry over from what is published:

- the model never writes a timestamp it did not read: every stamp in `content.md` is one that exists
  in the capture, and the check holds it to that
- segment into topics first, then read each chapter, then write `gist` and `open` last and
  de-duplicate; a single pass neglects the middle of a two-hour call

The digest reads the manual's outline and the people table before the capture, so it knows what we
act on: bias toward what changes how we operate, and toward speakers running the larger operation.
Recall target: everything in the owner's own notes of a call appears in that call's digest.

## 3. The manual — `knowledge/structured/`

One tree. `approved/` and `suggested/` merge; a bullet an agent wrote opens `(?)`, and vetting is the
owner deleting it. An agent never removes a `(?)` and never rewrites the words of a bullet without
one — it may move it, and may put it under a new `(?)` conclusion. `internal/` moves out to
`knowledge/internal/`, so what ships is a directory boundary.

Organised by the thing being operated, in the order the business meets it:

```
knowledge/structured/
├── market/        niche.md · city.md · niches/<trade>/…   (a trade's overlay mirrors this tree)
├── profile/       creation · naming · categories · verification/{video,live,instant,sab_to_pab} · suspension/
├── ranking.md     what moves rank: the signals, each pointing at the page that works it
├── reviews/       sourcing/{stand,customers,overseas} · rate_limits · replies · deletion · local_guide
├── site/          seo · conversion
├── calls/         phones · closing · resale
├── staff/         va
├── contractors/   sourcing · splits · contracts · pricing · payments
├── infra/         gmails · devices · proxies
└── regions/<country>/…
```

The tree follows the content: finalise it while moving, split a page that collects two topics.

A page states conclusions; who said what is evidence under them:

```md
# <topic>
<what we do here, as of now — the page's answer in a few lines>

## <a step or a decision, in the order it is met>
- <conclusion: reads true without knowing who said it>
  > qualifier
  - <evidence: who, what they ran or said, the number>
    <!--2026-09-25 Dante ran https://…?t=353-->

## open
- Q: / TODO:
```

- `info / facts / plays` go: `how` in the citation says what kind of statement it is
- a story no conclusion stands on does not enter the manual; it stays in its `content.md`, where
  search finds it
- `guides/` goes. The lead of a page is its guide, and `guide <area>` serves it. `experts.md` splits:
  the people table to `knowledge/README.md`, when and how to refer someone to the member skill
- `knowledge/README.md` is the one operating manual for `knowledge/`: what each section is, who
  writes it, the lifecycle above, the page and citation formats, the style, the tables. It absorbs
  `structured/README.md`; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` keeps the bird's-eye view and links it

## 4. Skills

```
skills/ingest/          capture · digest · propose · integrate, run in that order; each reads only what the one before wrote
  capture.md            code: pull, then watch — transcript, frames picked from what the speech says is shown, shown.md
  digest.md             → <capture>/content.md
  propose.md            → knowledge/log/digest/<date>-<capture>.md: each point worth keeping, the page it belongs on, what it changes there
  integrate.md          → the manual: for each proposal, rewrite / move / split / new page, so the page still reads as one text
  notes · people · internal · resolve      as today
plugin/skills/service-arb/   SKILL.md · experts.md
```

`distill` and `call-digest` are replaced by these, not kept beside them.

## 5. Migration (scripts in `./tmp/`, never `src/`)

1. spec, trust module, citation format, compile, server — the corpus converted mechanically
   (`r<n>` → `who how` needs the speaker: read it off the bullet's own attribution, and from the
   capture where the bullet names nobody; a citation that cannot be attributed is listed for the
   owner, not guessed)
2. digest every capture, most-cited first
3. rebuild the manual page by page from the old twin trees and `guides/`: old approved bullets keep
   their words as vetted evidence, everything written to bind them is `(?)`
4. delete `guides/`, `approved/`, `suggested/`, `distill`, `call-digest`; rewrite
   `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` to the shape above

## Verification

- one hook and one command, `playbook check`, over everything under `knowledge/`; `nix build` runs it
  and fails on: an old-form citation, a `who` with no table row, a stamp absent from its capture, a
  date after its capture's, a conclusion with no citation anywhere beneath it. Seed each with a broken
  fixture and see it refused. A capture with no `content.md` is pending work, not corruption: the
  hook lists it, the release build refuses it
- `playbook eval` on this tree against the last release: no case regresses; add a case whose answer
  needs a call speaker's trust, and assert the answer cites a number the server printed
- digest recall: digest the 2026-09-25 call and compare against the owner's notes of it
  (`~/tmp/meeting_notes.md`) — every note has a point
- read `contractors/splits.md` cold: it answers "what split do I offer a plumber" in its lead, without
  a name in the first line of any bullet
- `plugin/skills/service-arb/SKILL.md` contains no arithmetic and no number from a table

attribution, they are not redone from nothing.

```md
# <title>
- of: <capture> · digested by: <what>, <date>

## gist
who was on, what scale each operates at, what the call settled — a paragraph

## chapters
### [12:34](<url>?t=754) <topic>
- <point, in the speaker's terms; numbers, names, handles verbatim>
  <!--<who> <how> ?t=771-->
- Q: … / A: …

## open
questions nobody answered; things someone said they would do
```

No public prompt of Loom's or Fathom's exists; the skeleton above is theirs (purpose → topics with
seek links → open items) plus attribution. Two things carry over from what is published:

- the model never writes a timestamp it did not read: every stamp in `content.md` is one that exists
  in the capture, and the check holds it to that
- segment into topics first, then read each chapter, then write `gist` and `open` last and
  de-duplicate; a single pass neglects the middle of a two-hour call

The digest reads the manual's outline and the people table before the capture, so it knows what we
act on: bias toward what changes how we operate, and toward speakers running the larger operation.
Recall target: everything in the owner's own notes of a call appears in that call's digest.

## 3. The manual — `knowledge/structured/`

One tree. `approved/` and `suggested/` merge; a bullet an agent wrote opens `(?)`, and vetting is the
owner deleting it. An agent never removes a `(?)` and never rewrites the words of a bullet without
one — it may move it, and may put it under a new `(?)` conclusion. `internal/` moves out to
`knowledge/internal/`, so what ships is a directory boundary.

Organised by the thing being operated, in the order the business meets it:

```
knowledge/structured/
├── market/        niche.md · city.md · niches/<trade>/…   (a trade's overlay mirrors this tree)
├── profile/       creation · naming · categories · verification/{video,live,instant,sab_to_pab} · suspension/
├── ranking.md     what moves rank: the signals, each pointing at the page that works it
├── reviews/       sourcing/{stand,customers,overseas} · rate_limits · replies · deletion · local_guide
├── site/          seo · conversion
├── calls/         phones · closing · resale
├── staff/         va
├── contractors/   sourcing · splits · contracts · pricing · payments
├── infra/         gmails · devices · proxies
└── regions/<country>/…
```

The tree follows the content: finalise it while moving, split a page that collects two topics.

A page states conclusions; who said what is evidence under them:

```md
# <topic>
<what we do here, as of now — the page's answer in a few lines>

## <a step or a decision, in the order it is met>
- <conclusion: reads true without knowing who said it>
  > qualifier
  - <evidence: who, what they ran or said, the number>
    <!--2026-09-25 Dante ran https://…?t=353-->

## open
- Q: / TODO:
```

- `info / facts / plays` go: `how` in the citation says what kind of statement it is
- a story no conclusion stands on does not enter the manual; it stays in its `content.md`, where
  search finds it
- `guides/` goes. The lead of a page is its guide, and `guide <area>` serves it. `experts.md` splits:
  the people table to `knowledge/README.md`, when and how to refer someone to the member skill
- `knowledge/README.md` is the one operating manual for `knowledge/`: what each section is, who
  writes it, the lifecycle above, the page and citation formats, the style, the tables. It absorbs
  `structured/README.md`; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` keeps the bird's-eye view and links it

## 4. Skills

```
skills/ingest/          capture · digest · propose · integrate, run in that order; each reads only what the one before wrote
  capture.md            code: pull, then watch — transcript, frames picked from what the speech says is shown, shown.md
  digest.md             → <capture>/content.md
  propose.md            → knowledge/log/digest/<date>-<capture>.md: each point worth keeping, the page it belongs on, what it changes there
  integrate.md          → the manual: for each proposal, rewrite / move / split / new page, so the page still reads as one text
  notes · people · internal · resolve      as today
plugin/skills/service-arb/   SKILL.md · experts.md
```

`distill` and `call-digest` are replaced by these, not kept beside them.

1. spec, trust module, citation format, compile, server — the corpus converted mechanically

2. digest every capture, most-cited first
